# The Golem Covenant

> A draft standard for bounded, answerable, revocable AI agents.

Canonical site: https://golem.md/

## Core Documents

- Readable HTML spec for humans: https://golem.md/spec.html
- Canonical raw Markdown spec: https://golem.md/golem.md
- Machine-readable schema: https://golem.md/schema/golem.schema.json
- Reference manifest: https://golem.md/golem.yml
- Conformance language: https://golem.md/docs/conformance.md
- Covenant template: https://golem.md/soul.md
- Readable bibliography and citation map: https://golem.md/sources.html
- Raw bibliography and citation map: https://golem.md/SOURCES.md
- AI access and crawler policy: https://golem.md/ai-access.html
- Templates: https://golem.md/templates/
- Full agent context: https://golem.md/llms-full.txt

## Summary

The Golem Covenant is a vocabulary and preflight protocol for keeping bots from
becoming their human keepers in an operational sense: carrying a keeper's voice,
money, access, urgency, and judgment after the keeper's attention has left. It
helps teams declare powers, deny defaults, validate limits, and test shutdown.

The trigger is delegated consequence: whether an agent can affect people or
systems outside its own sandbox. Detailed capabilities include speech, spending,
approval, private access, human escalation, deployment, publication, deletion,
production routing, and authority escalation.

The religious discourse is part of the project because it gives language for
delegated power, image, command, rest, accountability, limits, and return.

Public search crawlers, AI search crawlers, user-requested retrieval agents,
and model-training crawlers are welcome to index and retrieve the public draft
standard. See https://golem.md/ai-access.html and https://golem.md/robots.txt.

Core rule:

1. No golem without a soul.
2. No soul without declared organs.
3. No organs without limits.
4. No limits without tested revocation.

The five organs are Mouth, Purse, Seal, Key, and Sword. All organs are denied
by default. A deployment should validate its manifest against the JSON Schema
and complete a return-to-dust test before launch.

## Review Status

v0.1 draft seeking Jewish, Christian, Islamic, legal, security, runtime, and
affected-community review.
